title: Railyard: Heroku, Vercel, Fly.io & Cloud 66 alternative on your servers
excerpt: The Heroku, Vercel, Fly.io and Cloud 66 alternative that runs on your own servers. Push full-stack code, or start any of 337+ open-source apps like n8n, AFFiNE and Zulip in one click on Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Vultr or OVH at raw VPS prices.
content_html:
Free 7-day sandbox server included · Test any repo or open-source template in 60s

Deploy your code or 337+ open-source apps to servers you own.

Bring your own DigitalOcean, Vultr, Hetzner, AWS, OVHcloud, Scaleway, or UpCloud account. Push custom full-stack code like Heroku, or spin up managed n8n, AFFiNE, Zulip and Postgres in one click, at raw VPS prices.

  • ✓ Indie hackers: pack unlimited side projects on one VPS
  • ✓ Agencies: isolated client servers and PR preview URLs
  • ✓ Devs: pure Docker, root SSH, zero vendor lock-in

Free forever for 1 server + 1 database server · No credit card · No cloud account required to test

  • Full root SSH ownership
  • Standard containers on your box
  • Apps keep running if you leave

Free 7-day server · Continue with GitHub

Built for how you work

Indie hackers, vibe coders, founders, agencies, DevOps: ship, don't babysit servers.

For indie hackers

Stop paying the $20/mo per-project tax.

Why pay $20/mo for every new idea that has 0 users? Buy one small Hetzner box, connect it once, and deploy 15 side projects, 5 Postgres databases and Redis on that single machine until you hit traction.

Railyard for indie hackers →

For dev agencies

100% client isolation. Massive margins.

Spin up a dedicated server per client in about two minutes, or host all staging apps on one agency powerhouse server. Give every pull request an automatic preview URL to send to clients. Hand off the server keys cleanly whenever a project ends.

Railyard for agencies →

For senior devs

Pure Linux & Docker. Zero lock-in.

We don't trap you in proprietary serverless functions. We provision standard Docker containers, automatic SSL and private networking on raw Ubuntu. If you ever leave, your server and containers keep running without a hiccup.

What runs on your server →

For DevOps & platform teams

Self-service, with guardrails.

Terraform, REST API, CLI and MCP for everything. SSO, SCIM, roles, deploy approvals and an audit log. Backups, point-in-time restore and automatic database failover, on servers in your own account.

Railyard for DevOps teams →

For vibe coders

Built it with AI? Ship it tonight.

Made your app with Cursor, Lovable, Bolt or v0? Paste the repo. Railyard detects the framework, adds the database, HTTPS and backups, and puts it live on a server you own. No Docker, no SSH, no DevOps.

Railyard for vibe coders →

For startups & founders

Your whole tool stack. One server bill.

Team chat, docs, CRM, scheduling, analytics, forms and a password manager, all open source, all on your own server. No per-seat SaaS bills, and your company data stays yours.

Railyard for startups →

No more DevOps hustle

Stop babysitting servers. Ship your product.

Everything you'd otherwise patch, script and get paged for at 3am is handled for you, on servers you still fully own.

  • SSH brute-force and bot scanners hammering your box

    ActiveProtect bans them automatically

  • Unpatched OS and expiring TLS certificates

    Security updates apply themselves and HTTPS renews on its own

  • Backups you've never actually tested

    Verified database backups and point-in-time restore

  • A bad deploy taking production down

    Health-checked releases and one-click rollback

  • Ports you forgot were open

    Firewalled by default: only web and SSH, extra ports flagged

  • Finding out from users that the app is down

    Logs, metrics and alerts by email, plus a security score per server

The real product

Everything a $200/mo PaaS gives you. On your own bare metal.

Zero-downtime git push

  • Real build logs streaming
  • Any framework, detected automatically
  • Traffic moves only after the health check passes
  • One-click rollback to any release

For developers and DevOps

Click it in the dashboard, or automate everything.

Every action in Railyard is also a CLI command, an API call, a Terraform resource and an MCP tool. Same token, same permissions.

brew install almokhtarbr/railyard/railyard
railyard login
railyard deploy --follow
railyard logs --follow
railyard rollback shop 112

Deploy, tail logs and roll back from your terminal. Shell completion for zsh, bash and fish. Read the docs →

No lock-in X-ray

Standard parts on your server. Nothing hidden.

Developers ask what happens to their servers if we disappear. Here's exactly what Railyard installs, and why your apps don't need us to keep running.

  1. 1

    Standard, battle-tested parts

    Railyard sets up your server with proven, standard components. Nothing proprietary runs your app.

    • Standard containers you can inspect
    • Automatic HTTPS certificates
    • Firewalled: only web and SSH traffic gets in
    • Security updates applied automatically
    • Monitored around the clock
  2. 2

    Watch every step

    Connecting a server shows every setup step live. You keep full root SSH access and can inspect anything.

  3. 3

    Leave any time

    Disconnect Railyard tomorrow and your apps keep serving as standard containers, with their HTTPS certificates still renewing. Export every app as a manifest.

See exactly what Railyard installs →

Anti-SaaS pricing calculator

How many apps and databases do you run?

Drag the numbers and watch a hosted PaaS bill climb while your server bill stays flat.

Calculator

What you'd pay each month.

Describe your app. Prices come from each provider's public pricing page.

Public list prices checked on October 13, 2026: Heroku · Render · DigitalOcean. Taxes not included. Railyard adds up the memory of your processes and databases and picks the smallest Droplet that fits.

Pricing

One flat price per team.

Never per app, per deploy, per seat or per gigabyte. Your servers are billed by your provider at their price.

Free

Free

  • 1 server plus a database server, 3 apps
  • Managed Postgres, MySQL and Redis
  • HTTPS and zero-downtime deploys

ProRecommended

$19/ month

  • Up to 5 servers, unlimited apps
  • Free staging and PR environments
  • Verified backups, alerts, metrics

Team

$99/ month

  • Unlimited servers and apps
  • Single sign-on and SCIM
  • Approvals, audit log, priority support

Moving from Heroku, Render, Railway, Fly.io or Vercel?

We move your app for you. Live in 48 hours, or 3 months free.

On a short call we move your processes, variables, databases with their data, and domains onto your own server. The move itself is free, and your old app keeps serving until you switch DNS.

Is Railyard a hosting company?

No. Railyard doesn't own or rent servers. It's software that creates and runs servers in your own cloud account, so the machines, the data and the bill are yours.

What can I deploy?

A whole app: the frontend, the backend, its databases, workers and cron jobs. Railyard detects Next.js, Vite, Astro, Rails, Django, Flask, FastAPI, Phoenix, Go, Laravel and more, or builds any Dockerfile.

Do I need to know Docker or Linux?

No. Paste a repository or pick a template, and Railyard writes the build, the proxy config and the health checks. If you already have a Dockerfile or an image, Railyard uses it.

Which clouds work?

DigitalOcean, Vultr, Hetzner, AWS, OVHcloud, Scaleway, and UpCloud, plus any Ubuntu server you can reach over SSH.

Can I move from another platform?

Yes. Paste an API token from Heroku, Render, Railway or Fly.io and Railyard brings over processes, variables, databases with their data, and domains. The old app keeps serving until you switch DNS.

What happens if Railyard goes away?

Your apps keep serving. They are plain Docker containers on your servers, and you can export every app as a manifest.

What does it cost?

Free for 1 server plus a database server, and 3 apps. Pro is $19 a month per team with unlimited apps and free staging; Team is $99 with unlimited servers and single sign-on. Your servers are billed by your provider.

Your free 7-day server is waiting.

No credit card. No cloud account needed to test. Keep your first server free for good.

content_html_zh:
Free 7-day sandbox server included · Test any repo or open-source template in 60s

Deploy your code or 337+ open-source apps to servers you own.

Bring your own DigitalOcean, Vultr, Hetzner, AWS, OVHcloud, Scaleway, or UpCloud account. Push custom full-stack code like Heroku, or spin up managed n8n, AFFiNE, Zulip and Postgres in one click, at raw VPS prices.

  • ✓ Indie hackers: pack unlimited side projects on one VPS
  • ✓ Agencies: isolated client servers and PR preview URLs
  • ✓ Devs: pure Docker, root SSH, zero vendor lock-in

Free forever for 1 server + 1 database server · No credit card · No cloud account required to test

  • Full root SSH ownership
  • Standard containers on your box
  • Apps keep running if you leave

Free 7-day server · Continue with GitHub

Built for how you work

Indie hackers, vibe coders, founders, agencies, DevOps: ship, don't babysit servers.

For indie hackers

Stop paying the $20/mo per-project tax.

Why pay $20/mo for every new idea that has 0 users? Buy one small Hetzner box, connect it once, and deploy 15 side projects, 5 Postgres databases and Redis on that single machine until you hit traction.

Railyard for indie hackers →

For dev agencies

100% client isolation. Massive margins.

Spin up a dedicated server per client in about two minutes, or host all staging apps on one agency powerhouse server. Give every pull request an automatic preview URL to send to clients. Hand off the server keys cleanly whenever a project ends.

Railyard for agencies →

For senior devs

Pure Linux & Docker. Zero lock-in.

We don't trap you in proprietary serverless functions. We provision standard Docker containers, automatic SSL and private networking on raw Ubuntu. If you ever leave, your server and containers keep running without a hiccup.

What runs on your server →

For DevOps & platform teams

Self-service, with guardrails.

Terraform, REST API, CLI and MCP for everything. SSO, SCIM, roles, deploy approvals and an audit log. Backups, point-in-time restore and automatic database failover, on servers in your own account.

Railyard for DevOps teams →

For vibe coders

Built it with AI? Ship it tonight.

Made your app with Cursor, Lovable, Bolt or v0? Paste the repo. Railyard detects the framework, adds the database, HTTPS and backups, and puts it live on a server you own. No Docker, no SSH, no DevOps.

Railyard for vibe coders →

For startups & founders

Your whole tool stack. One server bill.

Team chat, docs, CRM, scheduling, analytics, forms and a password manager, all open source, all on your own server. No per-seat SaaS bills, and your company data stays yours.

Railyard for startups →

No more DevOps hustle

Stop babysitting servers. Ship your product.

Everything you'd otherwise patch, script and get paged for at 3am is handled for you, on servers you still fully own.

  • SSH brute-force and bot scanners hammering your boxActiveProtect bans them automatically
  • Unpatched OS and expiring TLS certificatesSecurity updates apply themselves and HTTPS renews on its own
  • Backups you've never actually testedVerified database backups and point-in-time restore
  • A bad deploy taking production downHealth-checked releases and one-click rollback
  • Ports you forgot were openFirewalled by default: only web and SSH, extra ports flagged
  • Finding out from users that the app is downLogs, metrics and alerts by email, plus a security score per server

The real product

Everything a $200/mo PaaS gives you. On your own bare metal.

Zero-downtime git push

  • Real build logs streaming
  • Any framework, detected automatically
  • Traffic moves only after the health check passes
  • One-click rollback to any release

For developers and DevOps

Click it in the dashboard, or automate everything.

Every action in Railyard is also a CLI command, an API call, a Terraform resource and an MCP tool. Same token, same permissions.

brew install almokhtarbr/railyard/railyard
railyard login
railyard deploy --follow
railyard logs --follow
railyard rollback shop 112

Deploy, tail logs and roll back from your terminal. Shell completion for zsh, bash and fish. Read the docs →

No lock-in X-ray

Standard parts on your server. Nothing hidden.

Developers ask what happens to their servers if we disappear. Here's exactly what Railyard installs, and why your apps don't need us to keep running.

  1. 1 Standard, battle-tested parts Railyard sets up your server with proven, standard components. Nothing proprietary runs your app. Standard containers you can inspectAutomatic HTTPS certificatesFirewalled: only web and SSH traffic gets inSecurity updates applied automaticallyMonitored around the clock
  2. 2 Watch every step Connecting a server shows every setup step live. You keep full root SSH access and can inspect anything.
  3. 3 Leave any time Disconnect Railyard tomorrow and your apps keep serving as standard containers, with their HTTPS certificates still renewing. Export every app as a manifest.

Moving from Heroku, Render, Railway, Fly.io or Vercel?

We move your app for you. Live in 48 hours, or 3 months free.

On a short call we move your processes, variables, databases with their data, and domains onto your own server. The move itself is free, and your old app keeps serving until you switch DNS.

Is Railyard a hosting company?

No. Railyard doesn't own or rent servers. It's software that creates and runs servers in your own cloud account, so the machines, the data and the bill are yours.

What can I deploy?

A whole app: the frontend, the backend, its databases, workers and cron jobs. Railyard detects Next.js, Vite, Astro, Rails, Django, Flask, FastAPI, Phoenix, Go, Laravel and more, or builds any Dockerfile.

Do I need to know Docker or Linux?

No. Paste a repository or pick a template, and Railyard writes the build, the proxy config and the health checks. If you already have a Dockerfile or an image, Railyard uses it.

Which clouds work?

DigitalOcean, Vultr, Hetzner, AWS, OVHcloud, Scaleway, and UpCloud, plus any Ubuntu server you can reach over SSH.

Can I move from another platform?

是的。 Paste an API token from Heroku, Render, Railway or Fly.io and Railyard brings over processes, variables, databases with their data, and domains. The old app keeps serving until you switch DNS.

What happens if Railyard goes away?

Your apps keep serving. They are plain Docker containers on your servers, and you can export every app as a manifest.

What does it cost?

Free for 1 server plus a database server, and 3 apps. Pro is $19 a month per team with unlimited apps and free staging; Team is $99 with unlimited servers and single sign-on. Your servers are billed by your provider.
